results.title: Bank earnings to shed the first light on how higher yields are affecting the economy | Morningstar
results.content:
FactSet doesn't have a consensus estimate for Goldman's net interest income. Among the four banks at the top of the list with traditional deposit-gathering networks, JPMorgan Chase stands out with the highest expected sequential and year-over-year increases in net interest income.

What about credit quality rumblings? [...] "CRE is the first line of defense for most [smaller] banks," Marinac said. "Larger banks don't have as much CRE, but they do bigger deals. I think most banks, in this higher-rates environment, will show higher losses, but I do not think It will be substantial."

And it would seem that the largest banks don't see big trouble ahead - at least not yet.

(MORE TO FOLLOW) Dow Jones Newswires

10-12-26 0707ET [...] But for CRE loans on banks' balance sheets, the rate for criticized loans (those that are delinquent or appear unlikely to qualify for renewal) is closer to 4% or 5%, according to Marinac.

"We do have a credit cycle," he said. "But I think most banks have been stress-testing their CRE for several years now."
